title: How to Tell if Mice Are Inside the Walls

content_html:
Scratching inside a wall can come from mice, but pipes, ducts, and building materials can also make noise as temperatures change. To confirm rodent activity, look for a pattern of evidence: timing, droppings, rub marks, odor, and travel routes toward food or water.

Track when and where the noise repeats

Mice are often more active when the home is quiet, especially at night. Note the wall, height, and time of the sound over several days instead of opening a wall because of one isolated noise.

Look for evidence along room edges

Small droppings, gnaw marks, dark rub marks along baseboards, and damaged food support the diagnosis. Wear gloves during cleanup and avoid sweeping or vacuuming dry droppings in a way that sends contaminated dust into the air.

Check likely routes into the wall cavity

Inspect pipe penetrations, gaps under cabinets, and openings around wiring or baseboards. A small inspection camera or professional assessment can be more useful than cutting drywall without knowing the travel route.

Confirm activity before sealing an occupied cavity

Sealing every opening while animals remain inside can create odor, damage, or new escape holes. Combine monitoring, removal or targeted control, and then exclusion once activity has stopped.
